basic_identification.full_title: Reusable Sanitary Pad/Sanitary Napkin/Period Panties — Specification (First Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Textiles / Technical Textiles for Medtech Applications (approved by the Textile Division Council and finalized by the Technical Textiles for Medtech Applications Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Technical Textiles for Medtech Applications Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements, sizes, construction, performance, and testing schedules for reusable (multiple use) sanitary pads, reusable sanitary napkins, and period panties designed for external menstrual hygiene use.

revision_history.edition: First Revision (extensively revised to realign sizing, core dimensions, and absorbency categories; incorporate updated wash durability, restricted substances limitations, and all preceding amendments)

version_status_and_amendments.amendment_slips: No active amendments have been issued since the publication of this first revision copy.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Reusable Menstrual Hygiene / Medical Textiles)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Medical Textiles (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all reusable sanitary pads, sanitary napkins, and period panties manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must conform to IS 17514 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified reusable menstrual products in India is a punishable offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Micro and small enterprises are granted specific delayed implementation phases, and products manufactured by Self-Help Groups (SHGs) are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to technical and medical textile products.

requirements.detail: Every commercial pack of reusable sanitary pads/napkins/period panties must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) to verify conformity.

The composite product must consist of three primary layers to ensure moisture absorption and isolation: a) top cover or top sheet (for skin contact comfort); b) absorbent core (middle layer featuring highly absorbent woven/non-woven fabrics to retain fluid); and c) barrier or bottom layer (leak-proof backing layer to prevent fluid pass-through to outer garments).

requirements.requirement_type: Colour Fastness and Dimensional Stability of Raw Fabric
requirements.detail: The raw fabrics used for manufacturing must satisfy minimum colorfastness limits (to washing, rubbing, and acidic/alkaline perspiration) and show zero excessive shrinkage or elongation (dimensional stability to washing) as specified in Table 1.
The pH of the cold aqueous extract of the product must lie within a safe skin-compatible range when evaluated in accordance with IS 1390.

requirements.requirement_type: Ability to Withstand Pressure After Absorption
requirements.detail: The product must absorb standard volumes of colored distilled water (defined by size and capacity) and withstand a 1 kg standard load applied for 1 minute as per Annex B without showing any side or bottom leakage.

To prevent bacterial and fungal growth during repeated use, the total viable microbial count (bioburden) must not exceed 1 000 cfu/gm when tested per ISO 11737 (Part 1). Pathogenic Staphylococcus aureus must be completely absent when evaluated per IS 5887 (Part 2).

Under Amendment No. 3, to protect users from hormone-disrupting chemicals, the total individual or combined phthalate plasticizer levels in raw materials or finished products must be less than 0.1 percent when tested in accordance with IS 9873 (Part 6) at least once a year.

If required by the buyer, the raw materials must undergo biocompatibility evaluations (cytotoxicity, irritation, and skin sensitization tests under IS/ISO 10993 and IS 17932). If antibacterial properties are claimed, the fabric must demonstrate an antibacterial activity value of 2 or more initially and after the declared wash cycles when evaluated per IS/ISO 20743.

Grouped by identical materials, sizes, and manufacturing batches, random samples must be drawn per Table 2 for non-destructive and destructive testing to audit workmanship and absorption safety prior to lot acceptance.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 17514 : 2025 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification governing reusable (multiple use) sanitary pads, reusable sanitary napkins, and period panties designed for external menstrual hygiene use. Under India's statutory Medical Textiles Quality Control Order (QCO), all reusable menstrual hygiene products sold or imported in India must be certified by the Bureau of Indian Standards and bear the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to ensure safety. It outlines the essential three-layer product design (a soft top contact layer, an absorbent textile core, and a leak-proof back sheet) and establishes strict physical, chemical, and biological limits. These include standard colorfastness and dimensional stability of raw materials to withstand repeated washing, a safe skin pH range, liquid pressure resistance tested under standard load, a maximum microbial bioburden of 1 000 cfu/gm, complete absence of Staphylococcus aureus, and a maximum phthalate limit of 0.1 percent to prevent exposure to toxic plasticizers.
